title: Derived open/closed site mates retain sheaf restriction normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the exact etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. For an open immersion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], let $o_j:C_Xj_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C_U$ be the termwise canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and let $a_j:C_Uj_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^*C_X$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For a closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\delta_h:C_XRh_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{p,*}C_Z$ on $D^+$ be the specified counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and let $a_h:C_Zh_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_p^*C_X$ be canonical pullback comparison. Subscripts $e,p$ mean etale and pro-etale. Composition is read right to left.

Let $X$ be Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). For every open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the termwise $a_j,o_j$ on unbounded derived categories respect the derived open units $\eta_j^e,\eta_j^p$ and counits $e_j^e,e_j^p$:
$$j_p^*(o_{j,L})a_{j,j_{e,!}L}C_U(\eta^e_{j,L})=\eta^p_{j,C_UL},\qquad e^p_{j,C_XM}j_{p,!}(a_{j,M})o_{j,j_e^*M}=C_X(e^e_{j,M})$$
for all $L\in D(U_e,A)$ and $M\in D(X_e,A)$.

For every closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$, both $h_{e,*}$ and $h_{p,*}$ are exact. Let $\delta_h^0:C_Xh_{e,*}\to h_{p,*}C_Z$ on sheaves be the $h_p^*\dashv h_{p,*}$ transpose of $C_Z(\varepsilon^e_{h,L})a_{h,h_{e,*}L}^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon_h^\tau$ denotes the ordinary closed restriction/direct-image counit. Its termwise descent on $D^+$ is exactly $\delta_h$, under the exact-functor identifications $Rh_{\tau,*}=h_{\tau,*}$. Thus
$$\varepsilon^p_{h,C_ZL}h_p^*(\delta_{h,L})a_{h,h_{e,*}L}=C_Z(\varepsilon^e_{h,L})$$
for $L\in D^+(Z_e,A)$. The closed counits in this equation are invertible. Under them the restriction of $\delta_h$ is the identity of $C_ZL$; under the open units the restriction of $o_j$ is likewise the identity. These equalities use the canonical pullback comparisons, including their composition identifications.

proof.text: Use the canonical ordinary open unit equation of openComparison_unit_normalization. Compose its equality with restriction of the inverse extension comparison to obtain the unit-mate equation for the inverse extension comparison and the specified restriction comparison.

Localize the two ordinary open adjunctions using exactDerivedAdjunction. Its unit formula gives the normalized Hom formula exact_hom_fac on cochain representatives. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations give exactSquare_fac for the canonical restriction square. Apply derivedMate_comparison to these formulas and the degreewise ordinary unit-mate equation. Cancel the invertible target factorization and use localization natural-transformation extensionality to identify the actual derived inverse extension comparison as the inverse mate of the actual derived restriction comparison. Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm and mateEquiv_counit_symm, followed by cancellation of the inverse extension comparison, give both asserted open equations.

The ordinary open units are isomorphisms by full faithfulness of extension by zero. Exact localization takes their inverses and the canonical composition isomorphisms to an isomorphism from the composite derived extension/restriction to the identity. The localized adjunction therefore has fully faithful left adjoint, and its actual unit is invertible. Apply this to both sites, including the comparison image on the pro-etale side.

A closed immersion is finite, so its etale direct image preserves finite colimits by the existing finite-morphism exactness theorem. For pro-etale direct image take the open subscheme complementary to its closed range. Its inclusion is quasi-compact because the target is Noetherian. Its range is the complement of the closed range, so preservesFiniteColimits_lowerStar_of_isCompl applies. These arguments use all module sheaves, without constructibility hypotheses.

Apply the inverse counit formula for mates to the ordinary direct-image comparison. Its definition is an iterated mate of the sectionwise direct-image comparison. The iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm identity identifies the inverse mate with the specified canonical pullback comparison. Rewriting the adjunction Hom equivalence gives the asserted ordinary transpose formula.

Since both closed direct images are exact, their canonical right-derived-to-termwise isomorphisms satisfy the universal unit factorization. For the specified right-derived base-change transformation, apply localization extensionality on bounded-below homotopy representatives. Precompose with the invertible image of the right-derived unit and use rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac. Postcompose with the two exact-functor factorizations; naturality and the canonical exact-composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations reduce both sides to the same localized sheaf comparison. This proves the first closed equality for the actual specified maps.

The second closed equality is exactly fixedComparisonDirectImageMatePlus_counit, specialized to the closed immersion, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The ordinary closed counits are invertible by full faithfulness on both sites. Their termwise counits remain invertible on homotopy categories and bounded-below subcategories. The equation derivedPlus_counit_app_fac and invertibility of the right-derived unit for an exact functor show that each derived counit is invertible on the image of Qh. Essential surjectivity of Qh extends this to every object. The recorded derived adjunction equals derivedPlus by derivedAdjunctionPlus_eq_derivedPlus.
